messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: equivalent of CmdStan diagnose method in RStan?
parts:
The stan function takes an optional argument "diagnostic_file". I don't think I've ever used it (only in cmdstan), but it's definitely described in the documentation. From the stan function's help page:

diagnostic_file A character string of file name for specifying where to write diagnostics data for all parameters. If not provided, files are not created. When the folder specified is not writable, tempdir() is used. When there are multiple chains, an underscore and chain number are appended to the file name.

Ah ok. To test gradients in rstan you use the test_grad parameter. Also from the stan function's doc:

Another parameter is test_grad (TRUE or FALSE). If test_grad=TRUE, Stan will not do any sampling. Instead, the gradient calculation is tested and printed out and the fitted stanfit object is in test gradient mode. By default, it is FALSE.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] equivalent of CmdStan diagnose method in RStan?
parts:
Thanks, Jonah. I was specifically asking about the diagnostics that
are available with HMC, optimization and ADVI through CmdStan.
The fact that all four paths (what CmdStan calls "method", i.e.,
sample, optimize, advi, diagnose) all have diagnostic files
makes the terminology tricky.

In CmdStan, there's a separate diagnostics file produced (with unconstrained params
and other quantities I don't understand) for sampling, but it looks like there's
no programmatic way to get that info in R --- it just gets written to file (and
would have to be read back in with a generic R csv reader or something).

Daniel and I have been going through all the output to try to make
sure our writers are comprehensive enough.

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Consolidated-Output-for-Sample,-Optimize,-ADVI,-and-Diagnose

- Bob

In general the diagnostic output files report unconstrained values
and gradients (and momenta in HMC) to see everything going on
under the hood. This is additional information to the samples output
and not [HEAVY DUPLICATION]. But then I only wrote all the MCMC
code and writers, so what the hell do I know?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] equivalent of CmdStan diagnose method in RStan?
parts:
> On Mar 24, 2016, at 5:34 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> The diagnostic files have nothing to do with the “diagnose” method.

I couldn't find any doc on the "diagnostic_file" argument in the CmdStan
manual other than "Auxiliary output file for diagnostic information".
The Stan language manual doesn't appear to have anything unless
it's named something other than "diagnostic".

Daniel and I were trying to figure out what all the output was
and what all the input config is across RStan and CmdStan.

I couldn't find a way to call the "diagnose method" in RStan,
or find a way to get the "diagnostic files" other than as files.
So I was confusingly talking about both kinds of diagnosis.

> In general the diagnostic output files report unconstrained values
> and gradients (and momenta in HMC) to see everything going on
> under the hood. This is additional information to the samples output
> and not [HEAVY DUPLICATION].

The initial part of the file appears to be an exact duplicate of
the config output in the output.csv files, and several of the columns
appear to be the same (though maybe they're not --- I couldn't find any
doc). I guess whether that's "heavy" is in the eye of the beholder;
sorry if that was offensive, but I was just trying to mark duplicate
output so we could try to avoid some of the duplication going forward.

I realize there's new info there, too. It was confusing that
the name of the parameter was the same, but Daniel figured out it was
unconstrained when the values didn't line up with the output file.

There is also a diagnostic file output for ADVI and optimization, though
the one in optimization appears to only dump a dup of the config.

- Bob
